brief: AI capex and government borrowing are raising demand for capital while energy-driven inflation keeps policy rates high, pushing up the cost of capital: 30-year German and Japanese yields near zero in 2022 have risen sharply. Equity risk premia have fallen to late-1990s lows, so further yield increases threaten equities, though a 2-standard-deviation yield move (about 50bps a month) explains the recent pullback rather than the yield level itself. Earnings growth has offset the yield rise so far, pulling the S&P forward P/E from 22x to 19x, in line with its long-run average. Hyperscaler capex has eaten into free cash flow, pushing AA-rated capex growth to 65% year over year and record US IG issuance, and hyperscaler valuations have de-rated toward the market average. Not a valuation bubble, GS argues, but an earnings bubble is the risk, distinguished from 2008 banks by strong balance sheets, high interest coverage, and compute demand outstripping supply. GS is neutral equities over 3 months but overweight over 12, favoring diversification as US leadership fades and correlations fall.
